about: How a production-host answer is classed (2026-10-03 live fix item 3, review-2 P3-1/P3-2/P3-4). production_alias: a *.vercel.app host shaped like a project's production alias, claimable (the site-file proof decides). preview: refused as a production host. bare_platform: a deny suffix without its dot, refused. custom: not on the deny list, claimable. infinite-tag and the cloud must class every host here the same way.

cases.note: case and one trailing dot are normalised away
a digit in the first segment is never a hash
a 9-letter team slug with no digit is not a hash
KNOWN MISREAD (review-2 P3-1): a deployment URL whose hash has no digit reads as an alias; it fails safe on the proof (an old deployment never serves the new token)
a deployment URL (<project>-<9-char hash with a digit>-<team>)
a 9-char segment with a digit after the first reads as a deployment hash
KNOWN MISREAD (review-2 P3-1): a real alias with a 9-char digit segment reads as a deployment URL; the refusal says it LOOKS like a preview
more than one label under vercel.app (Vercel generates none)
a deny suffix without its dot: nobody's site, never provable (review-2 P3-2)
a deny suffix without its dot (review-2 P3-2)
a deny suffix without its dot (review-2 P3-2)
a look-alike is not on the deny list
